title: Coverage transitions are associated with different care-foregoing persistence routes

denominator.unit: recontacted respondents with complete care and coverage fields in both years

observations.method: Link 2024 and 2025 records by shedid; any Yes among E4_a-E4_f defines insured status and any Yes among E1_a-E1_e defines care foregoing; care paths and 2025 outcomes use 2025 panel_weight.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive selected panel comparison; no plan generosity, network, benefit, dated bill, causal direction, or replicate-weight standard errors.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable coverage can coexist with underinsurance, access barriers, illness, and affordability pressure.

denominator.unit: recontacted respondents with complete care and coverage fields in both years

observations.method: Link 2024 and 2025 records by shedid; any Yes among E4_a-E4_f defines insured status and any Yes among E1_a-E1_e defines care foregoing; care paths and 2025 outcomes use 2025 panel_weight.
observations.uncertainty: Small selected panel cell; no plan generosity, network, benefit, dated bill, causal direction, or replicate-weight standard errors.
observations.counterinterpretation: Coverage loss may be a marker of employment, eligibility, income, family, or health change rather than the cause of care foregoing.
